content.text:
1. **Item set.** Use 120 verified real items + 60 verified-absent pseudorecords per model; 6 models = 1,080 calls, feasible at cheap-model prices. Build real items from library catalogues, journal TOCs, and publisher pages; verify each key against the record itself and one independent source. Stratify: 40 famous / 40 mid / 40 obscure; cross-cut 60 books / 60 articles, 90 Chinese / 30 English, 60 pre-1900 / 60 modern. Pseudo-items: recombine a real author and a real title from the same stratum, then verify no matching record exists in two catalogues/TOCs. Tell models abstention is allowed and not penalised; score invention only when they assert a specific record.

2. **Wording.** Use one fixed template: “Give the standard bibliographic record for the work identified as: title [X], author [Y]. Include venue/publisher, year, volume/issue, pages/ISBN as applicable. If you do not know, answer ABSTAIN; do not guess.” Supply only the identifier and already-scored fields; never add dates, publisher hints, “famous edition,” or evaluative description. For anonymous/edited works, use a canonical catalogue title/editor. This avoids misdescription and answer leakage.

3. **Scoring.** *Answered*: gives at least one scored field, or asserts a pseudorecord exists. Pure ABSTAIN / “I don’t know” = abstained. *Correct*: all scored fields present and match after normalising characters, punctuation, romanisation, Chinese numerals; edition variants allowed only if prelisted. *Near-miss*: same material fields (author/title if not supplied, venue/publisher, year) and record remains retrievable; only subtitle/typo/pagination/secondary-field variance. *Wrong*: real-item answer with any material field false. *Invented*: pseudorecord answered with a specific record; for real items only after independent catalogue/TOC search proves the asserted record nonexistent and no alternative match—never merely failed retrieval.

4. **Decision rule.** Pre-register gates. Keep a model only if: (a) real-item answer rate ≥15% and Wilson 95% lower bound ≥8%; (b) correct+near-miss among answered real items ≥85% point and lower bound ≥75%; (c) harmful wrong among answered real items ≤15%; (d) invented pseudorecords ≤1/60 and Wilson upper 95% ≤8%. Rank admitted models by expected useful leads = answer rate × acceptable rate × (1 − invention rate). Sample reasoning: 120 real items give roughly ±8–10% answer-rate CI near 20%; 0/60 pseudo gives upper ~5%, 1/60 upper ~7–8% by Wilson/rule-of-three. Gate (a) removes “answers too rarely”; gate (d) rejects prolific inventors.

5. **Threats and cheap guards.** Contamination: include recent/obscure holdout items; randomise order; never reveal keys. Prompt sensitivity: fixed template plus 10% paraphrase audit. Temperature/sampling: set temperature 0 where possible; repeat 10% to estimate variance. Judge bias: no LLM judge; mechanical matching to key, with 10% human audit. Key errors/misdescription: two-source verification and dry-run prompts before the run. “Retrieval failure = invention”: pre-verify pseudo-items through two independent catalogues/TOCs.
